summary: ICP Connect is a scholarship scheme of VLIR-UOS, the Flemish universities' development cooperation body, for people from 25 countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America. It supports study in accredited English-taught international programmes at Flemish universities and university colleges: two professional bachelors, seven initial masters and three advanced masters in the 2027-2028 call. The scholarship covers the whole programme (12, 24 or 36 months) and is paid through the host institution; candidates apply to the institution for both the programme and the scholarship.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must hold the nationality of one of the 25 listed countries and live in one of them when they apply. The country of residence need not be the country of nationality. Eligibility depends on nationality and current residence, not on where a previous degree was earned. A person with two nationalities applies as a national of an eligible country and must live in a listed country.

The age limits are counted on 1 January of the intake year: bachelor and initial master candidates must be no older than 35, advanced master candidates no older than 45, and bachelor candidates must be at least 19.

Preference goes to candidates who work in higher education, government or civil society, or who aim for a career in those sectors. Recent graduates and private-sector candidates without experience can be considered if their motivation and profile are strong. Work experience is not required. Preference also goes to candidates who have not studied at bachelor or master level in a higher-income country; a short exchange there does not count against the applicant.

Only one ICP Connect scholarship can be applied for per year, and only one ICP programme. The applicant must not receive another scholarship or grant for the same study. They must not have had a Belgian government scholarship before, and must not have been enrolled at a Belgian higher education institution before 1 January of the intake year. If someone starts a programme without a scholarship, they cannot apply for a VLIR-UOS scholarship from the second year on. Being admitted without a scholarship does not stop a later application.

Advanced masters are generally for people who already hold a master; some accept a four-year bachelor, so the institution should be asked. A bachelor in an unrelated field may be accepted for specialised programmes when the person has relevant work experience. Programmes may add their own criteria.

All programmes are taught in English, so applicants must meet the English requirements set by each institution. Some programmes waive the test for those who studied in an English-speaking institution, and acceptance of online tests such as IELTS depends on the programme. Dutch is not required.
age_experience_notes: Age on 1 January of the intake year: at most 35 for bachelor and initial master, at most 45 for advanced master, at least 19 for bachelor. Work experience is not required; people working in higher education, government or civil society are preferred.
funding_summary: The scholarship covers the whole length of the programme: 12 months for a one-year programme, 24 months for a two-year programme and 36 months for a three-year programme. The framework sets a monthly study allowance of EUR 1,400 that includes living costs, board and lodging, health insurance, installation costs, indirect travel costs and tuition. A return economy flight at the start and end is added, and three-year bachelor students get one extra round trip. The scholar has no direct financial relation with VLIR-UOS; the Flemish host institution pays. There are no partial scholarships and no extensions.
programmes_note: Twelve programmes carry a scholarship in 2027-2028: professional bachelors in Hotel Management and Applied Computer Science; initial masters in Aquaculture, Food Technology, Marine and Lacustrine Science and Management, Transportation Sciences (Road Safety), Nutrition and Food Systems, Sustainable Land Management and Tropical Biodiversity and Ecosystems; advanced masters in Development Evaluation and Management, Globalisation and Development, and Governance and Development. Scholarships are only offered for programmes listed on the VLIR-UOS website. Eight other ICP programmes are still running but have no scholarship in 2027-2028. French-taught programmes are covered by another Belgian provider (ARES).
institutions_note: Programmes are run by Thomas More (Geel), VIVES (Noord), Ghent University, KU Leuven, Vrije Universiteit Brussel, University of Antwerp and Hasselt University. The institution reviews and ranks eligible applications; VLIR-UOS then screens the institution's selection list.

benefits.limit_text: EUR 1,400 per month (study allowance in the VLIR-UOS framework), paid for 12, 24 or 36 complete months
benefits.conditions: Covers meals, personal transport, personal expenses and accommodation, plus installation costs and study supplies. It is not a salary. If the scholar graduates after the first exam period, the remaining allowance is still paid. Two- and three-year programmes may allow a summer break approved by the programme; the allowance continues but extra tickets are not paid.

benefits.limit_text: Standard tuition fee for full-time enrolment, at the lowest applicable rate
benefits.conditions: Included in the monthly allowance. Depending on the institution, the scholar pays it from the allowance or the institution pays directly and deducts it. Language classes are not covered by tuition and come from the allowance.

benefits.limit_text: Health insurance (including liability, personal injury and repatriation cover) from the day of departure
benefits.conditions: Included in the monthly allowance; the institution helps arrange it and the scholar must be able to prove cover.

benefits.limit_text: One economy return ticket to Belgium at the start and one back at the end; one extra round trip for three-year bachelor students
benefits.conditions: Local legs of the itinerary included; no business or first class, no excess luggage, and no travel or visa costs for family members. Travel between Flemish campuses is reimbursed only in officially recognised interinstitutional programmes (Food Technology, Marine and Lacustrine Science, Sustainable Land Management, Water Resources Engineering).

benefits.limit_text: Board and lodging are paid from the monthly allowance
benefits.conditions: The host institution should help find affordable housing; early termination of a rental contract is the scholar's cost unless VLIR-UOS approves.

benefits.limit_text: Visa application fees, legalisation, medical certificates and transport to the embassy are included in the allowance
benefits.conditions: Extra visa or legalisation travel can be reimbursed with receipts only when the embassy is in another country or needs an overnight stay (per diem up to EUR 30 and lodging up to EUR 50 per night, up to 10 days). A social support fund can help with unforeseen emergencies, with VLIR-UOS consent.

benefits.limit_text: Extra funds for activities such as Global South immersions; partial scholarships; extensions
benefits.conditions: Some programmes may have their own funds for activities. Work is allowed only a few hours per week and not during compulsory classes.

requirements.text: Application to the chosen programme through the organising institution's admission process, with the scholarship request ticked on the programme application. There is no application fee.

English proficiency proof as set by the institution; some programmes waive it for applicants who studied at an English-speaking institution, and acceptance of online tests (for example IELTS) varies by programme.
Diploma or, until the final diploma is available, a temporary certificate or official transcripts where the programme accepts them.
Reference letters are part of the institution's admission process; none are needed separately for the scholarship.
requirements.conditional_rule: If the institution asks for them

requirements.text: Legalisation of documents through Belgian embassies or consulates may be needed for applicants from some countries; the institution gives details.

application_steps.title: Check eligibility and choose one programme
application_steps.detail: Read all the criteria (nationality and residence in one of the 25 countries, age, no earlier Belgian government scholarship, no enrolment at a Belgian higher education institution before 1 January of the intake year). Only one ICP Connect programme can be applied for per year, and only programmes listed by VLIR-UOS carry a scholarship.

application_steps.title: Apply through the institution for programme and scholarship
application_steps.detail: Follow the instructions on the organising institution's site and indicate the scholarship request on the programme application. Application dates differ by programme; the call page gives a general deadline of 28 February 2027, with earlier dates for several programmes (for example 15 January 2027 for Applied Computer Science and 30 November 2026 for Tropical Biodiversity and Ecosystems). There is no application fee.

application_steps.title: Prepare English proof and certified study papers
application_steps.detail: Meet the institution's English requirement, send transcripts or temporary certificates if the diploma is not yet issued, and expect reference letters to be collected in the admission process. An online information session ran on 26 November from 14:30 to 16:30 CET, with registration needed.

application_steps.title: Institution ranks all eligible applicants
application_steps.detail: The organising institution reviews and ranks every eligible application. The scholarship criteria are motivation and commitment to being an agent of change in sustainable development, professional experience and likelihood of using the new skills, gender balance (women strongly encouraged), regional balance, preference for vulnerable groups among equally qualified candidates, and preference for people who have never studied on a scholarship in a higher-income country.

application_steps.title: VLIR-UOS screens the shortlist and notifies by email
application_steps.detail: VLIR-UOS screens the selection list it receives from the institution and emails selected and waiting-list candidates no later than mid-May. Applicants who are neither selected nor waitlisted are informed by the programme they applied to.

application_steps.title: Study with a progress requirement and receive support through the host
application_steps.detail: The host institution pays the allowance and arranges insurance and ticket details. In two- and three-year programmes the scholar must pass at least 42 ECTS after the first year (and 84 ECTS after the second year in three-year programmes) to keep the scholarship; the programme, the institution and VLIR-UOS decide. Scholars may work only a few hours a week and not during compulsory classes.

application_steps.title: Postponement and early end
application_steps.detail: For urgent medical reasons a scholarship can be postponed or, rarely, prolonged with a doctor's certificate and VLIR-UOS approval requested through the programme. The scholarship covers only the full programme length; partial scholarships and extensions are not available.
